cards.text: Friend, the prophet Isaiah has a new message from the LORD: a burden against Damascus, the capital of Aram (Isaiah 7:8). I'll be honest, nobody's getting a thank-you card in this one. The LORD opens with what's become of the city.

cards.question: What does the LORD say Damascus has become?

cards.text: Damascus isn't the only place emptied out. The cities of Aroer are forsaken, and all that open space is about to get some new residents.

cards.question: Who moves into the forsaken cities of Aroer?

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says the fortress will disappear from Ephraim, Aram's ally (Isaiah 7:2), and the sovereignty from Damascus. Two kingdoms, same bad news.

cards.question: The LORD says what's left of Aram will be like the splendor of which people?
In that day, the LORD says, the splendor of Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28), will ___.

cards.text: And the fat of Jacob's body will waste away. The LORD compares it to a reaper gathering the standing grain with his arm, like someone gleaning heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.

cards.question: True or false: After the reaping, the LORD says gleanings will still remain.

cards.text: The LORD says it will be like an olive tree that has been beaten: two or three berries atop the tree, four or five on its fruitful branches. That's my chocolate chip jar after I "taste-test" a batch, and the only suspect has a MUSTACHE.

cards.question: But in that day, people will look up. Men will look to their ___ and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
True or false: When men turn their eyes to their Maker, they'll keep looking to the altars they made with their own hands.

cards.text: In that day, their strong cities will be like forsaken thickets and summits, abandoned to the Israelites and to utter desolation. And the message spells out why.

cards.question: Why will the strong cities end up like forsaken thickets? The message says, you have ___ the God of your salvation.

cards.text: And failed to remember the Rock of your refuge, too. I spent years forgotten in a junk drawer, friend, but forgetting the God who saves is a darker drawer than mine.

Then a garden picture: though you cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines, and help your seed sprout on the very morning you plant it. Somebody's hovering over that garden like I hover over the oven window.

cards.question: Though you tend that garden so carefully, what does the message say will happen to the harvest?

answers.text: a flood will sweep it away

cards.text: The harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain. Then the message gets LOUD: many peoples raging like the roaring seas, rumbling like the crashing of mighty waters.

cards.question: True or false: When the raging nations are rebuked, they stand their ground.

cards.text: They flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale. All that roaring, and they scatter like the crumbs on my counter when I sneeze.

cards.question: The message says sudden terror comes in the evening. When are the raging nations no more?
True or false: The message calls that sudden end the portion of those who loot and plunder.
